ana_01.label: Dataset profile — 5 comparison tables + registry + crosswalk
ana_01.content: Seven files. Four commercial ranking systems (THE 2603 rows/2011-2016, ARWU 4897/2005-2015, CWUR 2200/2012-2015, QS 1422/2023) plus a neutral open research-output anchor (OpenAlex, 600 institutions, fetched 2026-06-24), a Leiden CC0 registry (1506 rows, name/ROR/country only) and an 818-row school->country crosswalk. One row = one university's placement in one system. The only fully overlapping cross-SYSTEM edition year is 2015: THE has 401 rows for 2015, ARWU 500, CWUR 1000. QS (2023) and OpenAlex (current) are recent-state overlays, which is the dataset's central era-mismatch limitation (see ana_11).

ana_01b.label: Data-quality quirks in the join-relevant columns
ana_01b.content: Four quirks the downstream analysis handles explicitly. (1) THE 2015 stores 200 of its 401 ranks as BANDS ('201-225', '351-400'...); ARWU and QS band their tails too. code/common.py collapses a band to its lower bound. (2) QS 'score scaled' is numeric for only ~500 of 1422 schools (922 are blank/banded) and 308 QS ranks are ties ('6='). (3) OpenAlex two_yr_mean_citedness has exactly one anomaly: University of Washington at 46.4 versus a peer median of 3.39 — a data artefact, so use cited_by/works for per-paper impact instead. (4) CWUR indicator columns are RANKS (1=best), the OPPOSITE direction to the 0-100 scores in THE/ARWU/QS, and CWUR broad_impact is null for 2012-2013.

ana_02.label: Methodology weights — the perception-to-output axis
ana_02.content: The mechanical reason the tables disagree, encoded from the published methodologies (detective det_02..det_07). Reputation-survey share of the total score: QS 50% (Academic Reputation 40% + Employer 10%), THE 33% (15% teaching survey + 18% research survey) but with a further 30% on citations, ARWU 0%, CWUR 0%. OpenAlex is 0% reputation by construction (raw output only). Along a perception->measured-output axis the systems fan out QS (most perception) -> THE -> ARWU/CWUR (most output), with OpenAlex the pure-output anchor beyond them. This is a lookup, not a CSV computation, but it is the causal spine that ana_04/ana_07 confirm empirically.

data_table.description: Published weighting of each system (% of total score), reputation-survey share highlighted

ana_03.label: Cross-system name join sizes — 218-institution 5-way core
ana_03.content: A normalized-name join (code/common.py: lowercase, strip parentheticals/'university'/'the'/'of', de-accent, plus a small alias map for Ann-Arbor/ETH/EPFL variants) reproduces the dataset's advertised common core. Pairwise overlaps: THE n ARWU 297, THE n CWUR 354, THE n QS 306, THE n OpenAlex 280, ARWU n CWUR 439, CWUR n QS 587 (largest), QS n OpenAlex 453. The 2015 trio (THE n ARWU n CWUR) is 285; adding QS gives a 238-school 4-commercial core; adding OpenAlex gives the 218-institution FIVE-WAY common core. That 218 is slightly larger than the README's stated ~189 because this normalizer recovers more true variants (Michigan-Ann Arbor, ETH Zurich, University College London); the exact count is normalizer-dependent, so treat ~200 as the scale, not a precise constant.

ana_04.label: The 4 systems correlate only 0.60-0.85 (Spearman)
ana_04.content: On the 218-school common core, the six pairwise rank correlations between the commercial systems span Spearman 0.599 to 0.853 (Kendall 0.426 to 0.706) — 'correlated but far from agreeing', exactly the 0.7-0.8 band the literature reports (det_08). The two most alike are ARWU and CWUR (Spearman 0.853) — unsurprising, since both are survey-free research tables. The two LEAST alike are CWUR and QS (0.599), and QS's other two pairings are also the weakest (QS-ARWU 0.647, QS-THE 0.735): QS, the reputation-survey pole, is the systematic outlier. NB QS's low correlations partly reflect its 2023 edition vs the others' 2015 (see ana_11).

ana_05.label: Rank spread across the 4 systems — median 122 places
ana_05.content: For each of the 218 core universities, the gap between its best and worst rank across the four systems (max-min) has median 122.5 and mean 157.8 places (quartiles 63.8 / 122.5 / 210.0; max 850). The systems AGREE tightly only at the very top: Stanford varies by just 2 places (THE 4 / ARWU 2 / CWUR 2 / QS 3), Cambridge and Chicago by 3, Harvard and Penn by 4, MIT by 5. The biggest raw swingers are mid-tier schools whose spread is partly inflated by tail bands — George Mason (THE 351 / ARWU 151 / CWUR 414 / QS band 1001 = 850 spread), University of Technology Sydney (678), Syracuse (574). See ana_05b for the recognizable, band-free swingers.

ana_07.label: Which table tracks measured output — ARWU/CWUR closest, QS loosest on impact
ana_07.content: Correlating each commercial rank against the neutral OpenAlex order on the 218 core: ARWU and CWUR (the survey-free research tables) track it most closely on every lens, ARWU peaking at Spearman 0.876 against h_index and 0.775 against raw works. THE tracks raw volume LEAST (0.623) — not because it is reputation-heavy but because its citations pillar is size-normalized, so citation-dense Caltech outranks sprawling volume giants. QS tracks measured IMPACT least (0.636 vs h_index) — consistent with its 50% reputation weighting. Crucially, even the best correlation (0.88) is far from 1.0: no commercial table is 'just measuring output', so OpenAlex does not vindicate any single one.

ana_09.label: Reputation vs research — the survey lifts different schools
ana_09.content: Within QS itself, the Academic-Reputation survey score and the Citations-per-Faculty score correlate only Spearman 0.421 across the 218 core — the survey and the citation metric rank schools very differently. Comparing QS to ARWU on schools both rank <=200: QS lifts reputation-rich Asia-Pacific names far above ARWU's research-and-prizes order — University of Hong Kong (ARWU 151 / QS 21), NUS (101/11), Peking (101/12), Tsinghua (101/14), Seoul National (101/29). The reverse (ARWU >> QS) lifts US research-heavy schools — Vanderbilt (ARWU 53 / QS 199), Maryland (43/164), UCSB (38/149), Florida (83/188), WashU St Louis (32/118). Inside QS's own indicators, its reputation metric most over-lifts famous names with thin per-faculty citations (NYU AR 95.9 / CPF 28.9; Toronto 99.6 / 43.5; TU Munich 84.0 / 25.8), while its citation metric lifts research-dense but less-famous schools (Dartmouth AR 19.2 / CPF 86.7; Rensselaer 8.4 / 70.5; Bern 30.3 / 98.3).

ana_10.label: Size-normalisation flip — volume crowns Michigan, per-paper crowns Harvard
ana_10.content: Whether 'best research' means volume or per-paper impact flips the winner completely. By raw works_count OpenAlex crowns University of Michigan (980,174 works) but its citations-per-work is only 67.2 (impact rank #332) — a +331-place flip. Toronto flips +55 (volume #5, impact #60). At the other pole, small citation-dense schools soar when you divide by output: Caltech is volume #82 but per-paper impact #13 (-69), Princeton volume #104 / impact #24 (-80), MIT volume #35 / impact #3 (-32). Harvard is the rare school that is both big and dense (volume #2, per-paper impact #1). This is det_13's Caltech-vs-Michigan two-sided illustration, quantified: the same neutral database ranks the 'best' completely differently depending on one normalisation choice.

ana_11.label: VALIDATION — the disagreement survives holding the year fixed at 2015
ana_11.content: Robustness check for the era mismatch (det_14). Restricting to the SAME-YEAR 2015 trio (THE n ARWU n CWUR, 285 schools, all 2015 editions), the three systems still only agree at Spearman 0.757 (THE-ARWU), 0.751 (THE-CWUR) and 0.840 (ARWU-CWUR), mean 0.782 — NOT ~1.0. So the headline 'they disagree' is not an artefact of mixing years; it holds within a single year. LEVEL VALIDATED: cross-system methodology disagreement among the three 2015 tables (era held fixed). LEVEL THE HEADLINE CLAIMS: the full 4-way QS/THE/ARWU/CWUR disagreement plus the OpenAlex referee overlay. GAP: QS is 2023 and OpenAlex is 2026, so every QS- or OpenAlex-involving comparison conflates methodology divergence with an ~8-year (QS) / ~11-year (OpenAlex) time gap. QS's lower mean correlation (0.660 vs the trio's 0.782) is therefore an UPPER bound on its methodology divergence, not a clean estimate — the Editor must not sell a QS-vs-2015 gap as pure methodology.

ana_12.label: INTERACTIVE — re-weight the rankings and watch #1 flip
ana_12.content: The centrepiece client model. Each of the 218 common-core universities carries five REAL 0-100 pillars — rep (QS Academic Reputation survey), cite (THE field-normalised citation impact), teach (THE teaching), intl (THE international outlook), vol (OpenAlex raw output scaled 0-100). A pure-JS function blends them under reader-set weights and re-ranks. Just moving between five preset weightings produces THREE different #1s: balanced weights crown Oxford (87.02), a QS-like reputation-heavy weighting crowns MIT (96.25), and an output-only weighting crowns Michigan (100.0). A THE-like blend also gives MIT; an ARWU-like output blend gives Michigan. The reader discovers first-hand that 'best university' is a slider position, not a fact. Verified identical in Python and Node (code/client_model.js).

caveats.content: ERA MISMATCH (the dataset's main limitation): THE/ARWU/CWUR are 2015 editions, QS is 2023, OpenAlex is fetched 2026-06-24. The clean cross-SYSTEM comparison is the 2015 trio (ana_11, which validates the disagreement holds within one year). Any QS- or OpenAlex-involving figure conflates methodology divergence with an 8-11 year time gap and should be framed as a recent-state overlay, not a same-year comparison.

FUZZY NAME JOIN: the cross-system core is built on a normalized-name match (code/common.py), not a shared identifier, for the four commercial tables. It required a small manual alias map (Michigan-Ann Arbor, ETH Zurich/EPFL, TU Munich) and still produces a handful of genuine collisions where 'University of X' and 'X University' or homonyms collapse together: York (Univ of York UK vs York University Canada), Newcastle, Miami (Ohio vs Florida), China/Taiwan homonyms (2-7 collisions per system). The 5-way core is 218 here vs the README's stated ~189 — the exact count is normalizer-dependent; treat ~200 as the scale. OpenAlex and Leiden do carry ROR ids for a cleaner future join.

OPENALEX SIZE/COVERAGE BIAS: works_count rewards big, old, medical-heavy universities (Michigan #1, Sao Paulo top-10), so it is a yardstick of research QUANTITY, not quality — always read cited_by_count and h_index alongside it (ana_08, ana_10). Coverage is also uneven by region (documented discrepancies for China, det_06/det_14). One clear artefact: University of Washington's two_yr_mean_citedness = 46.4 vs a peer median of 3.39, which also inflates Washington's h_index rank (#1 by h_index) — flagged, not used for per-paper impact (cites/work used instead).

RANK BANDS INFLATE SPREAD: THE bands ranks past 200 ('201-225'), ARWU past 100, QS deep tails ('1001-1200'); code/common.py maps a band to its lower bound. This inflates the max-min spread for tail schools, so the raw 'biggest swingers' (George Mason 850, etc.) are partly artefacts. ana_05b restricts to schools ranked <=200 by all four systems for the recognizable, band-free swingers — use those for the story.

MIXED SCORE DIRECTIONS: CWUR's indicator columns are RANKS (1=best), the opposite direction to the 0-100 scores in THE/ARWU/QS, and CWUR broad_impact is null for 2012-2013 (present 2014-2015). All correlations here use each system's world_rank (a consistent rank space), never mixes raw scores across systems. The QS 2023 edition uses the pre-2024 LEGACY weights (Academic Reputation 40%), so its reputation-heaviness is specific to this edition.
